pr.title: Leave a replied question open, and let its agent revise it
pr.head: b227d00cd159be1c2b702ec1088915e1b596e19e

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent ask you a question with options, or tell you something, from inside a Claude Code session. Each item shows in the band, the panel above your prompt. Picking an option fills your prompt with the quoted question and that option's text. When you send the prompt, the band records the answer and delivers it to the agent as a message that starts ANSWER.

Before this change, the band recorded any text under a quoted question as the answer. The first line you typed became a typed answer, and the question left the band. In practice a reply is often a question back or a clarification, so that resolved questions that still needed you.

• Only an option answers. The band records an answer only when the text after a quoted question, up to the next quoted item or the end of the prompt, is exactly one of its options. Anything else is a reply: the band records nothing, closes the drawer, and the question stays open.
  • The agent settles a replied question. The Projector section of AGENTS.md and the ask tool's description tell the agent to answer what you asked, then withdraw, revise, or leave the question open.
  • Agents can revise a question in place. A new project inbox revise command and a revise tool replace an open question's text and keep its number, pull request, asking subagent, and snooze.

Two review rounds have run. The first found that answering one of two questions with the same subject also counted as a reply to the other. The fix merges the answer and reply rules into readPrompt, which gives each quote in a prompt to one question. The same commit records discuss as a pick and keeps a pick made before a revision from answering any question. The review of this head found it clean.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Band: Projector's panel above the Claude Code prompt that lists pull requests and inbox items.
  • Drawer: the expanded view of one item in the band, with its detail and numbered options.
  • Proposal: the option a drawer put in the prompt, which the band remembers so a quote goes to the right one of two questions with the same subject.
  • Reply: anything sent under a quoted question that is not exactly one of its options.
  • Stale pick: a proposal made before its question was revised. Sent as it stands, it replies to the revised question and answers nothing.

cards.title: Can revise forge an answer?
cards.html: No. inbox.revise writes only subject, choices, and detail, under the session's lock, and refuses any item with an answer recorded, including one claimed for delivery. The band matches an option by its text, not its letter, so a revision that reorders options cannot change what a pending pick means.

groups.title: Revising a question in the store
groups.kicker: A new project inbox revise command that rewrites an open question in place
intro: The inbox stores each item as a JSON file per session, and every write happens under the session's lock. revise is a new write beside answer, dismiss, withdraw, and snooze. It replaces only the parts it is given and runs the same checks ask runs on the result.
It refuses a notice, a resolved question, an answer letter such as 3.a, and a revision with nothing to change, each with exit 65. An unknown number exits 66, and a busy lock exits 75.

checks.text: A revision cannot overwrite your answer: record raises when the item has an answer, before it changes anything. ReviseTests passes, and the full Python suite ran OK on this head.

files.note: Adds the revise parser, with --option and --no-options mutually exclusive, and dispatches to inbox.revise.

groups.title: Which prompts answer a question
groups.kicker: readPrompt gives each quote in a prompt to one question, as an answer or a reply
intro: When you send a prompt, the band reads it for quoted inbox items. readPrompt splits the prompt at each quote and reads the text up to the next quote. That text answers a question only when it equals one of the question's options, ignoring surrounding whitespace. Any other text is a reply. A typed answer under the last letter is no longer produced from a prompt.

Each quote goes to one question. When two open questions share a subject, an option goes to the question whose drawer last put that option, or the bare quote through discuss, in the prompt, and otherwise to the oldest that offers it. A reply goes to the question whose drawer put the quote there, and otherwise to the oldest. A stale pick, made before its question was revised, replies to the revised question and answers nothing.
The ask, withdraw, and new revise tool descriptions live in the same file.

files.note: Replaces answersIn with readPrompt, which returns both answers and replies. Adds replyNote and the revise tool's description, schema, and argument builder.

checks.text: An answer to one of two questions with the same subject no longer replies to the other. A temporary test on this code gave the answer to question 2 alone, with no replies. That was the review's earlier finding, now fixed.

Suppose you press discuss on one of two questions with the same subject, its agent revises it, and you type an option. That stale discuss pick does not hold the text back, so the option answers the other question. On main, a typed option under a shared quote also goes to the oldest question, so this is not a regression. The review lists it as a suggestion.
reviseArguments passes each value in its flag's = form, so text that starts with - stays text, and an empty options list becomes --no-options.

groups.title: The band's prompt handler and revise tool
groups.kicker: How a sent prompt closes drawers, and how revise redraws a question
intro: The band's prompt handler takes answers and replies from readPrompt. It closes only the drawers of the questions the prompt answers or replies to, and of the notices and resolved questions it quotes. For a subagent's question it adds a relay note for an answer, or a reply note for a reply, so the main loop knows whom to forward the prompt to.

propose records what a drawer put in the prompt, now including discuss as an empty answer, along with the quote as it read then. The revise tool runs project inbox revise, puts the revised question in the band at once, and marks that question's picks stale rather than dropping them, so an old pick cannot fall through to another question with the old words.

files.note: Registers the revise tool, adds propose, and reworks the prompt handler around readPrompt.

checks.text: A pick ends once a prompt you send answers or replies to its question, or holds the quote it was made under.
A revision marks picks stale instead of dropping them, so readPrompt can recognize the old text and hold it back.

groups.title: What the agent is told
groups.kicker: The Projector section of AGENTS.md moves to begin marker 11
intro: The generated Projector section tells every agent how to treat a reply: answer what the person asked, then withdraw the question if the reply settles it, revise it if it was unclear or the choice changed, or leave it open. The template's text is pinned by hash, so the version moves from 10 to 11.
